dmitri: Quick heads-up — I repro an OOM regression after switching the default attention path to the new FlashAttention kernel on A100s when users have long prefix KV. Setup: seq_len=2048, batch=2, head_dim=64 (8 heads), dtype=fp16. We see workspace allocation failures in the runtime; logs show large temporary workspace requests that blow past free memory :warning:

lena: Can you paste the profiler snippet / allocator log? Sounds like a workspace-sizing heuristic is requesting too much temp memory. FlashAttention has a big temp cost at certain window sizes. :thinking:

dmitri: Pasted profiler + allocator trace below:
```
[profiler] kernel=FlashAttentionV2 seq=2048 batch=2 heads=8 head_dim=64 dtype=fp16
requested_workspace_bytes=3435973836  # ~3.2GB
allocator: try_alloc(3435973836) -> failed
allocator: largest_free_block=2874540200  # ~2.67GB
OOM: fallback not attempted, request raised as error
stack: attention_forward -> runtime_dispatch -> workspace_manager::alloc
```

alex: That matches a bug we saw earlier: our workspace heuristic computes temp as "per_tile * num_tiles" without capping against a sane per-GPU fraction. Two practical fixes: 1) kernel-specific clamp (e.g. max_workspace = min(config.max_workspace, floor(0.8 * free_mem))) 2) automatic fallback to alternate kernel (Triton FA/legacy or cuBLASLt matmul path) when alloc fails. We should avoid immediate OOM and try a lower-memory kernel first.

rob: Also note KV cache behavior: for prefix-heavy workloads the KV cache itself occupies a lot of persistent device memory. We were naively calculating workspace as if KV would be swapped out. We should account for live KV usage: live_kv_bytes + requested_workspace <= usable_gpu_memory. If not, prefer a kernel with smaller transient footprint or route to dedicated node.

lena: Agreed. Proposed heuristic prototype: choose kernel by (seq_len, batch, head_dim, dtype, live_kv_bytes) -> picks preferred kernel and a max_workspace_bytes. Example rule: if seq_len>1024 and live_kv_bytes>1GB then prefer TritonFA with workspace clamp 512MB; else FlashAttention up to 1.5GB. We'll microbenchmark to pick thresholds.

dmitri: Also seeing allocator fragmentation in logs — even when total_free > requested_workspace we still fail because largest contiguous block is too small. Two allocator tunings to try: pre-allocate a workspace arena per-stream for attention kernels (contiguous), and run a periodic compact/merge pass after large frees. Could also try buffer reuse across attention->ffn (reuse same temp buffer region if lifetimes don't overlap).

alex: For buffer reuse: add a small lifetime-analysis pass in the runtime planner that marks temporaries as "reusable" and places them in a shared workspace pool. Start with conservative rule: only reuse when tensors are same dtype and size within 10%. This drastically reduces peak transient demand in some traces.

perf-bot: quick microbench snapshot (latest run):
```
run=1769876500: GPU=A100 40GB, batch=2, heads=8, head_dim=64
seq_len 256: FlashV2=12.3ms, TritonFA=14.8ms, workspace=128MB
seq_len 1024: FlashV2=45.2ms, TritonFA=52.6ms, workspace=640MB
seq_len 2048: FlashV2=98.1ms (wksp=3.2GB, alloc_fail 3/10), TritonFA=135.4ms (wksp=512MB, stable)
```

lena: Nice. That shows tradeoff: Flash gives perf but risks OOM at high seq lengths. Actionable plan: 
- implement kernel-specific workspace clamps (runtime config + env override) :memo:
- fall back sequence: Flash -> TritonFA -> cuBLASLt matmul path before erroring
- allocator changes: per-stream arena for attention kernels + simple compaction pass
- add metrics: workspace_alloc_fail_count, kernel_fallback_count, peak_transient_bytes, largest_free_block_gauge
- prototype buffer-reuse planner for attention->ffn pass

dmitri: I'll start a PR with a small change: add clamp + fallback on alloc failure and expose config flags. Will also add runtime metric for alloc_fail. Assigning to @lena for the heuristic table + microbench harness.

rob: I can scope the allocator arena patch and tests. We'll need a regression test that simulates live_kv_bytes plus large seq len to ensure fallback triggers instead of hard OOM.

alex: One more safety thing: if fallback chain exhausted, return a structured error recommending route: reduce seq length, use streaming decode, or route to Dedicated capacity with larger GPU. We should avoid opaque OOMs.

lena: +1. I'll draft the threshold grid and run sweeps over head_dim and batch in the next 24h.

dmitri: Thanks everyone. I'll link the initial PR here once ready. :thumbsup:
